clue.text: Cherish the sound grass left by the birds

parts.note: to cherish someone is to love them

indicators.note: the word sound tells us to take a word for grass as it is spoken, giving a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass

explanation.surface: Someone treasures the noise of grass deserted by the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds' is British slang for young women, so being left by the birds means jilted. LAWN said aloud gives LORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovelorn means pining for a lost love, as a man abandoned by his girlfriends would be.

clue.text: Lady in distress, like Miss Languish?

indicators.note: distress suggests disorder, so the letters are put in disarray

explanation.surface: A damsel in trouble, resembling a stage heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Lydia Languish is the romantic heroine of Sheridan's play The Rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydian here means resembling Lydia, the first name of the heroine of The Rivals.

clue.text: Condescend to go bail for Peter

parts.note: to go bail for someone is to vouch for them
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Lowering oneself to stand surety for a man named Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name; in thieves' slang it is a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouchsafe is to grant graciously, as from a superior to an inferior.

clue.text: Calm flustered bay with a soporific

parts.note: to lull is to calm

indicators.note: flustered means agitated, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Settling an agitated bay with something to send it to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a song sung to send a baby to sleep.

clue.text: Mechanical sort of chap is right about, instrument having no base.

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the right abbreviation goes round the rest
the base letter e, as in natural logarithms, is removed from the instrument

parts.note: the oboe is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: An engineer type who is correct about a musical device without a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no base' drops E (the base of natural logarithms) from OBOE to leave OBO, which RT goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine built to resemble and act like a person.

clue.text: French writer holding, little daughter — the one who had teething troubles

definitions.text: the one who had teething troubles

indicators.note: the writer's name holds, or contains, another piece inside it

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French novelist
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A French author with a small girl, and someone whose teeth gave him grief.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Cadmus sowed a dragon's teeth, which sprang up as armed men: hence his comic 'teething troubles'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Theban founder planted dragon's teeth that grew into warriors, a humorous kind of trouble with teeth.

clue.text: Swore the bible had gone astray

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
to have erred is to have strayed from the right path

explanation.surface: Took an oath that the holy book had been lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert firmly, as one would under oath.

clue.text: Isle of Grain getting major road

parts.note: malt is processed grain
an A road is a major road in Britain

explanation.surface: A Kent peninsula is getting a big new road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Grain is a peninsula in Kent, England, which makes 'Isle of Grain' read as one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Mineral supplied for party ceremony

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Minerals provided for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Siderite is an iron carbonate ore.

clue.text: It's crazy, taking one drug on top of another!

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits above the next, so the first drug is written first

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: A warning that mixing drugs is madness.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric person, and as an adjective means mad or absurd.

clue.text: This description of a Lee-Enfield is purely nominal

definitions.text: This description of a Lee-Enfield is purely nominal

parts.words: This description of a Lee-Enfield is purely nominal
parts.note: a Lee-Enfield is a single-barrelled rifle, but its hyphenated two-part name is like a posh two-part surname, so the gun term applies only to the name

explanation.surface: A remark that a rifle's label describes only its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated surname such as Smith-Jones is called this, a term borrowed from guns with two barrels.

clue.text: A stymie in opposition

parts.note: to stymie someone is to thwart or obstruct them

explanation.surface: A golfing obstruction placed to oppose a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart means across or against, in a contrary direction.

clue.text: Privateer, rough in speech and demeanour

indicators.note: in speech asks us to hear the word for rough spoken rather than read it

parts.note: rough means coarse
an air is a person's manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: A pirate described as crude in both his talk and his bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: COARSE said aloud gives the sound CORS, which is then followed by AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate or privately owned raider licensed to attack shipping, especially on the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Peeress's joint title

parts.note: a peeress is a lady, so of the peeress is the lady's
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A title shared jointly by peeresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint title' reads as a shared title; in fact 'joint' is the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Your Ladyship is the form of address used for a woman of noble rank.

clue.text: Stick bills here to make a saving

explanation.surface: Advice on where to post notices and save money.
explanation.definitionFit: A billboard where posters are pasted, and the act of putting by a stockpile.

clue.text: The old man's Continental bedding

parts.note: du is French for 'of the', the possessive supplied by the 's
a vet, short for veteran, is an old man

explanation.surface: Dad's European quilt.
explanation.walkthrough: DU VET reads as French for 'of the veteran', i.e. the old man's. A duvet was long called a 'continental quilt' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A duvet is a quilt filled with down, which British shops once sold as a continental quilt.

clue.text: Give clear order, like a governor

indicators.note: to order letters is to arrange them, here in a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Issuing an unambiguous command, as a ruler would.
explanation.definitionFit: Viceregal describes a viceroy, a governor ruling a colony on the monarch's behalf.

clue.text: Book first class up to the general assembly

parts.note: Eccles is an abbreviation of Ecclesiastes, a book of the Bible

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first class

explanation.surface: Reserving top-tier seats for a big meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecclesia was the popular assembly of citizens in ancient Athens.

clue.text: Tributary to an Indian king

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Paying homage to a native chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tributary' looks like a payer of tribute to the king; it is a small river.
explanation.definitionFit: A creek is a stream, especially one feeding a larger river.

clue.text: He makes chips for a kipper, it is said

indicators.note: it is said shows the word is heard, so a same-sounding spelling is used

parts.note: one who kips, or naps, is a napper

explanation.surface: A man who fries potatoes to go with smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' looks like smoked fish, but it means one who kips, or sleeps. A knapper chips flint into tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapper shapes flint by striking off flakes.

clue.text: A model craft — it's made by human hand

indicators.note: to model clay is to shape it anew, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A scale-model boat crafted by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' rearranges CRAFT and IT into RTIFACT, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is any object produced by people rather than by nature.

clue.text: Supporter put down ticket money with a flourish

parts.note: a fan supports a team
a fare is the price of a travel ticket

explanation.surface: A football fan pays for a ticket with a showy gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a short burst of trumpets announcing someone.

clue.text: Ankle covering makes one walk with hesitation

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Something worn on the leg causes a person to falter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaiter is a cloth or leather covering for the ankle and lower leg.

clue.text: Find common ground with a : type of Scot

parts.note: common means vulgar or low
ground means land

explanation.surface: Agreeing with a certain kind of Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lowlands are the southern part of Scotland, as opposed to the Highlands; 'Find common ground' looks like a phrase meaning agree.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lowland Scot comes from southern Scotland, the counterpart of a Highlander.

clue.text: Incongruous part of the Merry Widow's wardrobe?

definitions.text: Incongruous part of the Merry Widow's wardrobe?

parts.words: Incongruous part of the Merry Widow's wardrobe?
parts.note: a widow traditionally wears black mourning clothes, which sit oddly on a cheerful widow like the heroine of Lehar's operetta

explanation.surface: A joke about the clothes of an operetta heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Widow's weeds are the black clothes a widow wears in mourning.

clue.text: The smallest sea creature a little island can produce

parts.note: min, short for minimum, is the smallest amount
an orca is a killer whale

explanation.surface: A tiny marine animal bred on a small isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca, the smaller of the two main Balearic Islands, takes its name from Latin for lesser.

clue.text: This insect is a little fellow without a tail

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a midget is a very small person

explanation.surface: A small bug likened to a tiny tailless man.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a small biting gnat.

clue.text: In great gulps he'd drunk the drugged mixture

indicators.note: something drunk is befuddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down a spiked potion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges IN, GREAT, GULPS and HED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose of liquid medicine taken to induce slumber.

clue.text: Mop sailor's eye

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
orb is a poetic word for the eye

explanation.surface: A seaman's eye cleaned with a mop.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up liquid is to soak it up.

clue.text: Radical republican who wanted to get even

explanation.surface: A revolutionary seeking revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Levellers were 17th-century English radicals who wanted equal rights; one who 'gets even' sounds like a revenge seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levellers were a radical faction in the English Civil War, and literally someone who makes things flat or equal.
